Wars with Wadai in the west, ended by Tayrab's treaty; eastward expansion into Kordofan under Muhammad Tayrab, held until the Turco-Egyptian conquest (GHA V ch.7 p.189); conquered by al-Zubayr 1874 (GHA VI ch.14 p.371).

Key events
  • Fur dynasty from around Jabal Marra; Sulayman Solongdungu probably the founder; the Kayra sultanate flourished c.1640–1874, restored 1898, annexed 1916 (GHA V ch.7 p.187); O'Fahey (2008) dates it c.1650–1916 (page not confirmed) VERIFY
  • Muhammad Tayrab takes Kordofan from the Musabba'at; it stays with the Fur until the Turco-Egyptian conquest (GHA V ch.7 p.189)
  • Permanent capital grows at al-Fashir under 'Abd al-Rahman (d. 1801–2) (GHA V ch.7 pp.190–191)
  • Sultan Ibrahim defeated and killed by al-Zubayr at Manawashi, 1874; Darfur annexed to the Turco-Egyptian regime (GHA VI ch.14 p.371)
  • Ahmad Bukr b. Musa (c.1682–1722) pushes north and north-west, annexing Dar Kimr; the Kayra meet the Zaghawa and Wadai source
  • The eunuch Muhammad Kurra, Ab Shaykh, is from about 1790 to 1804 the strongest man in the Fur state source
  • W. G. Browne stays in Darfur 1793–6 and describes the sultan as the chief merchant of the country source
  • Sultan 'Abd al-Rahman corresponds with Bonaparte in 1799 during the French occupation of Egypt source
  • On 'Abd al-Rahman's death in 1801–2 his son Muhammad al-Fadl succeeds with the help of Muhammad Kurra source

AllianceConflictTradeSubjugationMigration

  • Sulayman Solongdungu, probably the dynasty's founder, drove out the Tunjur and annexed the area around Jebel Marra. SINGLE-SOURCE [medium] · relation · Conflict
    1640 CE – 1874 CE

    Al-Fashir → Ain Farah (Wikidata Q405860)

    Sources: Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot, The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V) (1992), pp.187–188

  • Sultan Ya'qub of Wadai invaded as far as Kabkabiyya and was driven out; in the mid-18th century Wadai defeated 'Umar Lel's army and captured the sultan. SINGLE-SOURCE [medium] · relation · Conflict
    1640 CE – 1874 CE

    Al-Fashir → Ouara (Wara) (Wikidata Q1974522)

    Sources: Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot, The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V) (1992), p.188

    The Kayra consolidated their hold on Dar Zaghawa through marriage alliances and by backing one section against another, in competition with Wadai.

    No arrow: no anchor for "Zaghawa"

    Sources: Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot, The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V) (1992), p.188

  • Fur → Egypt (Forty Days Road) Trade SINGLE-SOURCE [medium]

    Darfur's long-distance trade to Egypt ran on the Darb al-Arba'in and was largely under state control.

    No arrow: no anchor for "Egypt (Forty Days Road)"

    Sources: Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot, The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V) (1992), p.183; Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot, The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V) (1992), p.187

  • Masalit → Darfur sultanate Subjugation SINGLE-SOURCE [medium]

    Before the Egyptian conquest of Darfur, Dar Masalit was part of Darfur's western district under the viceroy of the west; the Masalit had only firrash, lower-ranking chiefs.

    No arrow: group has no anchor (masalit)

    Sources: H.A. MacMichael, A History of the Arabs in the Sudan and some account of the people who preceded them and of the tribes inhabiting Darfur, Vol. I (1922), p.86

Dating note

Start c.1640 (GHA V ch.7 p.187). O'Fahey 2008 gives c.1650 (page not confirmed); earlier value 1603. GHA VI ch.14 p.356: the Kayra 'ruled Därfür until 1874'. Older chronologies place Sulayman earlier; founding date genuinely uncertain. El Fasher date c.1790–91. Tunjur end aligned to c.1640 (GHA V ch.7 pp.187–188).

حروب مع وداي غرباً؛ وتوسع شرقاً في كردفان نحو 1785؛ وفقدان كردفان بعد 1821؛ وفتحها الزبير 1874 (هولت وديلي، المقدمة ص1–9). [يحتاج تحقق]

أحداث رئيسية
  • أسرة فوراوية من منطقة جبل مرة؛ ولعل سليمان سولونج مؤسسها؛ ازدهرت سلطنة الكيرا نحو 1640–1874، وأعيدت 1898، وضُمّت 1916 (GHA V ch.7 p.187)؛ ويؤرخها أوفاهي (2008) بنحو 1650–1916 (الصفحة غير مؤكدة) يحتاج تحقق
  • التوسع في كردفان في عهد محمد تيراب نحو 1785 يحتاج تحقق
  • تثبيت العاصمة في الفاشر نحو 1790/1791 في عهد عبد الرحمن يحتاج تحقق
  • فتحها الزبير رحمة 1874 يحتاج تحقق
  • أحمد بكر بن موسى (نحو 1682–1722) يتوسع شمالاً وشمالاً غربياً ويضم دار قِمر، فيحتك الكيرا بالزغاوة ووداي يحتاج تحقق المصدر
  • الخصي محمد كُرّا، أب شيخ، أقوى رجل في دولة الفور من نحو 1790 إلى 1804 يحتاج تحقق المصدر
  • و. ج. براون يقيم في دارفور 1793–1796 ويصف السلطان بأنه كبير تجار البلاد يحتاج تحقق المصدر
  • السلطان عبد الرحمن يراسل بونابرت عام 1799 أثناء الاحتلال الفرنسي لمصر يحتاج تحقق المصدر
  • عند وفاة عبد الرحمن في 1801–1802 يخلفه ابنه محمد الفضل بمساعدة محمد كُرّا يحتاج تحقق المصدر

ملاحظة التأريخ

Start c.1640 (GHA V ch.7 p.187). O'Fahey 2008 gives c.1650 (page not confirmed); earlier value 1603. GHA VI ch.14 p.356: the Kayra 'ruled Därfür until 1874'. Older chronologies place Sulayman earlier; founding date genuinely uncertain. El Fasher date c.1790–91. Tunjur end aligned to c.1640 (GHA V ch.7 pp.187–188). يحتاج تحقق
